data.title: ADR-004: The CLI layer and the build
body: # ADR-004: The CLI layer and the build
- **Status:** accepted
- **Scope:** stack
## Context

ADR-003 freed the core of dependencies, but the CLI layer has jobs where an implementation of our own no longer pays off: parsing arguments, generating `--help`, suggestions on a typo in a command name.
## Alternatives considered
| Option | Pros | Cons |
| `cac` 7.0.0 | 3.3 ms — the cheapest of those tested; 41 KB; built-in `--help` | The project has long been without releases — a risk of abandonment |
| `citty` 0.2.2 | Actively developed (UnJS); 35 KB | 8.3 ms — twice as expensive; version 0.x, the API may still change |
| `commander` 15.0.0 | The de facto standard, the best documentation | 17.1 ms — 11% of the budget just for parsing arguments |
| Own parser | 0 ms | `--help`, subcommands and user errors are not 80 lines but a permanent debt |
## Decision
| Role | Choice | Why |
| Argument parsing | **`cac`** | The cheapest; the API is stable precisely because the project is finished |
| Colours | **own ANSI constants** | ~10 lines with a check of `NO_COLOR` and `isTTY`; `picocolors` costs 7.7 ms for the same thing |
| Tables | **own renderer** | Column widths for three fields; `cli-table3` pulls in `string-width` |
| Frontmatter | **own parser** | `gray-matter` is 13 ms and a dependency on `js-yaml`; we need to read a few `key: value` lines up to `---` |
| Build | **esbuild** | 147 KB, without dependencies; `tsup` is a wrapper that pulls in `cac`, `chokidar`, `consola` |
| Tests | **vitest** | A dev dependency, it does not affect the runtime budget |

On the risk of `cac`: it is localised in one module (M6), which only describes the commands and passes the parsed arguments into the core. Replacing the parser would not touch a single core module — that is a few hours of work, not a rewrite.
## Clarification of 2026-09-02 (from the result of the implementation)

**`cac` does not support multi-word commands.** The declaration `cli.command('task add <title>')` gets into `--help` and looks like it works, but no action is called: `matchedCommand` stays empty, and the CLI quietly exits with code 0. Found on the first end-to-end check.
The workaround is the pattern `task <action> [title]` with the action parsed inside the handler. The price: `--help` for a separate subcommand has to be written by us.

This does not change the decision: `cac` remains the cheapest by measurement (3.3 ms against 8.3 for `citty`). But the risk in the ADR was named wrongly — abandonment of the project was expected, and a limitation of functionality is what came true. If subcommands go beyond three levels, moving to `citty` will pay off.
## Consequences
- Positive: the total import cost of the runtime dependencies is 3.3 ms instead of 40+; the core remains fit for embedding as a library.

- Cost of the decision: own colours, tables and frontmatter are code that will have to be maintained; each of them has to be trivial, and if one of them starts to grow, that is a signal to take a library.
- What will have to be reconsidered: if `cac` stops working on a new major version of Node, we move to `citty` and pay 5 ms.
